title: Block Raises Full-Year Profit Forecast as Cash App Growth Accelerates
excerpt: Jack Dorsey's payments company beat Q2 estimates with adjusted EPS of $1.02 versus 87 cents expected, and lifted its 2026 gross profit outlook to $12.51 billion on the strength of Cash App and AI-driven cost cuts.
body:
• Block reported adjusted EPS of $1.02 in Q2, beating Wall Street estimates of 87 cents, and raised its full-year gross profit forecast to $12.51 billion (21% growth)
  • Cash App gross profit surged 31% year-over-year in Q2, while Square merchant business rose 13%
  • The company cut more than half its workforce in February as part of an AI-integration overhaul; CEO Jack Dorsey said Block is evolving into an "intelligence company"
  • Shares rose more than 4% in extended trading despite some concern about the pace of workforce reduction

Block raised its full-year gross profit forecast on Wednesday after the payments company posted second-quarter results that comfortably exceeded Wall Street expectations, driven by resilient consumer spending and accelerating growth at Cash App.

The Jack Dorsey-led company reported adjusted earnings of $1.02 per share for the three months ended June 30, well above the 87-cent consensus compiled by LSEG. Block now expects full-year gross profit of $12.51 billion, representing 21% growth, up from its prior forecast of $12.33 billion.

Cash App Leads the Way

Cash App, which has evolved from a peer-to-peer payments tool into a broader consumer financial services platform, was again the standout. Gross profit at the unit surged 31% in the quarter, building on the 38% growth it posted in Q1.

The platform's lending arm continued its rapid expansion. Consumer lending origination volume through Cash App Borrow had surged 82% in Q1 to $17.6 billion, and the momentum carried into the second quarter. Cash App Green, the company's premium banking tier, ended the prior quarter with 9.7 million primary banking actives, up 18% from a year earlier.

Square, Block's merchant-facing business, posted 13% gross profit growth in Q2 as it continued to benefit from payment volumes across both everyday essentials and discretionary spending.

The AI Restructuring Bet

Block's results come five months after the company announced it would cut more than half its workforce to embed AI across its operations — one of the most aggressive headcount reductions in the payments industry.

"Intelligence tools are the next major technology shift, but machine learning is not new to Block."

— Jack Dorsey, CEO, Block, in a letter to shareholders

The company has leaned heavily into AI tools internally. By mid-April, production code changes per engineer were running at more than 2.5 times the January rate. Builderbot, an internal agent, has reviewed more than 90% of production code changes and is making 15% of code changes nearly autonomously. On the customer side, Block has rolled out AI-powered tools like Moneybot for Cash App and Managerbot for Square sellers.

Dorsey told shareholders he believes Block is "evolving into an intelligence company," saying the roadmap is "no longer the limiting factor" in what the company can build.

Strong Payments Season

The results cap a broadly strong earnings season for the U.S. payments industry, with Visa and Mastercard also posting robust numbers. Consumer spending has remained resilient despite inflationary pressures from the Middle East conflict and elevated borrowing costs, with both discretionary and essential transactions flowing through the same payment networks.

The second half typically brings seasonal tailwinds from holiday shopping and events like Cyber Monday, which could further boost payment volumes.

What's Next

Shares rose more than 4% in extended trading but had already climbed roughly 9% this year as of the last close. The stock's trajectory depends on whether Block can sustain Cash App's growth rate and translate its aggressive AI bet into lasting margin expansion without sacrificing execution quality — a concern some analysts have raised given the scale of the workforce reduction.
nri_angle: Block's Cash App and Square platforms are widely used by Indian American entrepreneurs and consumers, and the company's AI-driven cost-cutting strategy mirrors trends across Silicon Valley.
